If the conductivity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.001</mo><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mtext> </mtext><mi>HA</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mtext> </mtext><msup><mi>cm</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, degree of dissociation of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>HA</mi></math> is

solution.text:
Kohlrausch's law states that the equivalent conductivity of an electrolyte at infinite dilution is equal to the sum of the conductances of the anions and cations.

λmoHA=λmoHCl+λmoNaA-λoNaCl

=425.9+100.5-126.4

=400

λmo=K×1000M=5×10-5×10310-3=50

α=50400=0.125
